questions.question_text: A client with schizophrenia has completed treatment at Pantang Hospital and is preparing to return to his community. Which intervention best demonstrates psychiatric rehabilitation?

choices.text: Keeping the client permanently in an institutional psychiatric facility
Supporting the client to develop daily living skills, obtain employment and participate in community activities
Restricting the client's contact with community members
Concentrating exclusively on the administration of antipsychotic medication

questions.rationale: Psychiatric rehabilitation aims to improve functioning, independence, social participation and quality of life through recovery-oriented interventions. Permanent institutionalisation, social restriction and medication-only management fail to address the client's broader rehabilitation needs.

questions.question_text: A man recovering from a severe depressive episode wishes to return to his previous occupation but fears discrimination from colleagues. What should the community mental health nurse prioritise?

choices.text: Advise him to abandon his employment plans
Arrange supported employment and engage relevant stakeholders in reducing workplace stigma with the client's consent
Recommend permanent withdrawal from social activities
Advise him to conceal all his difficulties and avoid follow-up care

questions.rationale: Supported employment promotes independence, recovery and social inclusion while addressing discrimination through appropriate advocacy. Abandoning employment, social withdrawal and avoiding follow-up reinforce exclusion and undermine recovery.

questions.question_text: Which statement accurately describes public stigma associated with mental illness?

choices.text: The internalisation of negative beliefs about oneself because of mental illness
Negative stereotypes, prejudice and discriminatory behaviour directed towards people with mental disorders
The acceptance of individuals with psychiatric conditions into society
The development of coping skills by psychiatric clients

questions.rationale: Public stigma occurs when members of society hold negative stereotypes, develop prejudicial attitudes and discriminate against people with mental disorders. Internalised stigma refers to the person's adoption of negative societal beliefs, while the other options describe acceptance and recovery-related processes.

questions.question_text: The family of a client with schizophrenia believes that the illness results entirely from witchcraft and refuses to support prescribed treatment. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Criticise the family's cultural beliefs and terminate the discussion
Provide culturally sensitive psychoeducation about schizophrenia, treatment adherence and relapse prevention
Encourage the family to discontinue psychiatric treatment
Exclude the family from all rehabilitation activities

questions.rationale: Family psychoeducation improves understanding of mental illness, treatment adherence, early recognition of relapse and supportive caregiving. Criticism, withdrawal of treatment and unnecessary family exclusion can increase stigma and weaken the client's support system.

questions.question_text: Which principle is central to recovery-oriented psychiatric rehabilitation?

choices.text: The complete elimination of every psychiatric symptom before community participation
The individual's involvement in directing personal recovery goals and decisions
The permanent transfer of decision-making authority to healthcare professionals
The restriction of clients to hospital-based activities

questions.rationale: Recovery-oriented care recognises the client's autonomy, strengths, preferences and ability to pursue meaningful life goals even when some symptoms persist. The other options promote dependency, unnecessary institutionalisation and unrealistic expectations of complete symptom elimination.

questions.question_text: A community mental health nurse visits a client with bipolar disorder who has stopped attending follow-up appointments and discontinued prescribed medication. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Discharge the client from community mental health services
Assess the client's current mental state, medication-related concerns, safety and barriers to follow-up
Immediately report the client to the police
Assume that the client no longer requires psychiatric care

questions.rationale: A comprehensive assessment identifies possible relapse, adverse effects, treatment concerns and barriers to accessing care. Discharge, unnecessary police involvement and assumptions about recovery may expose the client to preventable deterioration.

questions.question_text: A client recovering from schizophrenia is unable to prepare meals, manage personal hygiene or organise daily activities independently. Which rehabilitation intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Structured activities of daily living training
Permanent restriction of independent activities
Exclusive use of pharmacological treatment
Complete withdrawal of family involvement

questions.rationale: Activities of daily living training develops practical skills required for independent living and community functioning. Permanent restrictions, medication-only care and withdrawal of appropriate family support do not adequately address functional limitations.

questions.question_text: Which organisation is primarily responsible for providing the national framework for mental health governance and protecting the rights of persons with mental disorders under Ghana's Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846)?

choices.text: Mental Health Authority
Ghana Education Service
National Road Safety Authority
Ghana Tourism Authority

questions.rationale: The Mental Health Authority is established under Act 846 to oversee and coordinate mental health services and promote the rights of persons with mental disorders. The other institutions have mandates unrelated to national mental healthcare governance.

questions.question_text: A community mental health nurse identifies a client with schizophrenia who is becoming increasingly withdrawn, sleeping poorly and expressing suspicious beliefs about neighbours. What is the most appropriate priority intervention?

choices.text: Wait until the client develops severe psychotic symptoms before intervening
Conduct an urgent mental state and risk assessment and arrange appropriate clinical review
Encourage the client to stop all prescribed medication
Recommend that the family conceal the behavioural changes

questions.rationale: Increasing withdrawal, sleep disturbance and suspiciousness may indicate an emerging psychiatric relapse requiring prompt assessment and clinical review. Delaying intervention, discontinuing medication and concealing symptoms may increase the risk of deterioration.

questions.question_text: A community leader publicly describes people discharged from Accra Psychiatric Hospital as dangerous and unsuitable for employment. Which community intervention would most effectively address this attitude?

choices.text: Exclude people with mental disorders from community gatherings
Organise evidence-based mental health education and recovery-focused contact involving people with lived experience
Encourage community members to avoid discharged psychiatric clients
Restrict mental health information to healthcare professionals

questions.rationale: Evidence-based education and meaningful contact with people who have lived experience can challenge stereotypes and reduce discriminatory attitudes. Exclusion, avoidance and restricted access to information reinforce stigma rather than promote inclusion.

questions.question_text: A caregiver reports that a relative with schizophrenia becomes increasingly sleepless, suspicious and socially withdrawn before previous relapses. What should the nurse teach the caregiver to do?

choices.text: Wait until the client becomes aggressive before seeking assistance
Recognise these changes as possible early warning signs and promptly contact the mental health team
Double the client's antipsychotic dose without consultation
Prevent the client from participating in all household activities

questions.rationale: Recognising individual early warning signs enables timely assessment and intervention, potentially preventing severe relapse. Waiting for aggression, independently changing medication doses and imposing unnecessary restrictions are unsafe responses.

questions.question_text: A client with a history of bipolar disorder has been discharged into a rural Ghanaian community. The family reports that the client has stopped sleeping, is spending excessively and is speaking continuously. Which action should receive the highest priority?

choices.text: Arrange an urgent psychiatric assessment because the findings suggest an emerging manic relapse
Encourage the client to undertake additional business activities
Advise the family to ignore the behavioural changes
Postpone clinical review until the next routine appointment

questions.rationale: Reduced need for sleep, excessive spending and pressured speech are characteristic warning signs of mania and require urgent psychiatric assessment. Additional stimulating activities, ignoring symptoms and delaying review may increase the risk of financial harm and clinical deterioration.

questions.question_text: Which intervention best illustrates the role of a community-based rehabilitation team in supporting a person with a long-term psychiatric disability?

choices.text: Providing medication without assessing social functioning
Coordinating healthcare, vocational training, family support and community participation
Maintaining the individual in residential isolation
Restricting rehabilitation to occasional hospital visits

questions.rationale: Community-based rehabilitation uses coordinated, multisectoral interventions to address health, education, livelihood, social participation and empowerment. Medication-only care, isolation and hospital-centred services do not adequately support comprehensive community rehabilitation.

questions.question_text: A community health officer at a CHPS compound identifies an adult with persistent low mood, loss of interest and hopelessness. The individual also reports thoughts of suicide. What should the officer do first?

choices.text: Arrange a routine health education session for the following month
Assess immediate suicide risk, establish safety and arrange urgent referral to an appropriate mental health service
Advise the individual to remain at home without follow-up
Recommend traditional treatment as the only intervention

questions.rationale: Suicidal thoughts require immediate assessment of intent, plan, means and protective factors, followed by appropriate safety measures and urgent clinical referral. Routine education, unmonitored home care and exclusive traditional treatment do not adequately address potential suicide risk.

questions.question_text: A client with schizophrenia states that although occasional auditory hallucinations remain, he wishes to resume education and develop friendships. Which response best reflects recovery-oriented nursing?

choices.text: Inform him that education is impossible until all hallucinations disappear
Collaboratively develop achievable educational and social participation goals while maintaining appropriate clinical care
Advise him to avoid relationships because of his diagnosis
Replace his personal goals with goals selected exclusively by the nurse

questions.rationale: Recovery-oriented care supports meaningful personal goals, autonomy and social participation while addressing ongoing symptoms through appropriate treatment. Requiring complete symptom elimination, discouraging relationships and disregarding client preferences undermine recovery principles.

questions.question_text: A client with severe depression is discharged from Ankaful Psychiatric Hospital. During the first community visit, the nurse discovers that the client has access to pesticides, has written a suicide note and is refusing to discuss safety. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Leave the client with relatives and arrange a review in one month
Initiate emergency suicide risk management, ensure continuous appropriate supervision and arrange urgent psychiatric intervention
Encourage the client to attend a community recreational activity
Concentrate on vocational rehabilitation before addressing suicide risk

questions.rationale: Access to a potentially lethal substance and a suicide note indicate an acute, high-risk situation requiring immediate safety intervention and emergency psychiatric assessment. Routine follow-up and rehabilitation activities cannot take precedence over preventing imminent self-harm.

questions.question_text: Which outcome provides the strongest evidence that family psychoeducation has been effective for a household caring for a person with schizophrenia?

choices.text: Family members prevent the client from making personal decisions
Family members recognise relapse indicators, support treatment adherence and communicate without hostility
Family members permanently withdraw from the client's care
Family members conceal the psychiatric diagnosis from all healthcare professionals

questions.rationale: Effective family psychoeducation improves illness understanding, relapse recognition, treatment support and constructive communication. Excessive control, abandonment and concealment of clinically relevant information undermine collaborative psychiatric care.

questions.question_text: A person with a psychiatric history is denied participation in a community development committee solely because of a previous hospital admission. Which concept best describes this action?

choices.text: Social inclusion
Discrimination
Psychiatric rehabilitation
Family psychoeducation

questions.rationale: Discrimination occurs when an individual experiences unfair treatment or exclusion because of a characteristic such as a mental health history. Social inclusion and rehabilitation promote participation, while psychoeducation concerns improving understanding of mental illness.

questions.topic: Traditional Healing Practices and Mental Illness in Ghana
questions.question_text: A client with schizophrenia informs a psychiatric nurse that he visits a traditional healer because his family believes his hallucinations have a spiritual origin. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Dismiss the client's cultural beliefs as irrational
Explore the client's beliefs respectfully while explaining the importance of evidence-based psychiatric treatment
Advise the client to discontinue prescribed antipsychotics
Prohibit all discussions about traditional healing

questions.rationale: Culturally sensitive nursing recognises the influence of spiritual beliefs while promoting safe, evidence-based treatment and therapeutic collaboration. Dismissal, discontinuation of medication and refusal to discuss cultural practices can damage trust and increase treatment disengagement.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse visiting a prayer camp in Ghana discovers that a person with severe psychosis is chained to a tree and denied adequate food and water. What should be the nurse's immediate priority?

choices.text: Accept the practice because it is culturally established
Assess the person's immediate medical and psychiatric condition, address life-threatening needs and activate appropriate safeguarding and referral procedures
Recommend longer periods of confinement
Leave without documenting the findings

questions.rationale: Chaining, dehydration and food deprivation expose the individual to serious physical and psychological harm and require immediate safeguarding, clinical assessment and appropriate referral. Cultural acceptance does not justify abuse or neglect, and continued confinement may worsen the person's condition.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine and Psychotropic Drug Interactions
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes a potential risk of combining herbal preparations with prescribed psychotropic medications?

choices.text: Herbal preparations always improve the effectiveness of psychotropic medication
Herbal constituents may alter drug metabolism, increase adverse effects or reduce therapeutic drug concentrations
Herbal medicines cannot affect the central nervous system
Combining herbal and psychiatric medications eliminates medication toxicity

questions.rationale: Herbal products may alter drug-metabolising enzymes and transporters or produce additive pharmacological effects, potentially causing toxicity or treatment failure. Their natural origin does not guarantee safety, and they do not automatically improve psychotropic treatment.

questions.question_text: A client with depression explains that she believes her illness is connected to ancestral displeasure. Which response demonstrates cultural competence?

choices.text: Your beliefs are wrong because depression has no cultural interpretation.
Can you explain what this belief means to you and how it influences your decisions about treatment?
You should abandon your beliefs before receiving psychiatric care.
Your family should decide your treatment without consulting you.

questions.rationale: Exploring the client's explanatory model helps the nurse understand cultural influences on illness perception and treatment decisions without reinforcing harmful beliefs. Dismissal, coercive cultural rejection and unnecessary removal of autonomy undermine culturally competent care.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Mental Health Legislation
questions.question_text: Which Ghanaian legislation provides legal protections concerning the treatment, dignity and rights of persons with mental disorders?

choices.text: Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846)
Road Traffic Act, 2004 (Act 683)
Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992)
Education Act, 2008 (Act 778)

questions.rationale: The Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846) provides the legal framework for mental healthcare and protection of the rights of persons with mental disorders in Ghana. The other legislation addresses road traffic, company regulation and education rather than mental health governance.

questions.question_text: A client with schizophrenia is brought from a prayer camp to a psychiatric facility with severe dehydration, multiple pressure injuries and persistent hallucinations. Which nursing intervention takes priority?

choices.text: Begin spiritual counselling before assessing the physical condition
Assess and stabilise the client's physical condition, address dehydration and pressure injuries, and arrange psychiatric evaluation
Return the client immediately to the prayer camp
Restrict fluids because the client has hallucinations

questions.rationale: Severe dehydration and pressure injuries require immediate physical assessment and treatment alongside psychiatric evaluation. Delaying medical treatment for spiritual counselling or returning the client to an unsafe environment may worsen preventable complications.

questions.topic: Traditional Healing Practices and Mental Illness in Ghana
questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse is discussing traditional healing with a family whose relative has depression. Which approach best supports collaborative mental healthcare?

choices.text: Encourage the family to replace prescribed antidepressants with unverified herbal mixtures
Discuss the family's treatment preferences, assess possible risks and encourage coordinated care that does not delay necessary psychiatric treatment
Refuse to involve the family in treatment discussions
Assume all traditional healing practices are harmless

questions.rationale: Collaborative care respects cultural preferences while evaluating safety, potential interactions and the need for evidence-based treatment. Replacing prescribed medication, excluding supportive relatives and assuming that every traditional preparation is harmless may expose the client to avoidable risks.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine and Psychotropic Drug Interactions
questions.question_text: A client taking an antidepressant reports starting St John's wort without informing the psychiatric team. What is the most important concern?

choices.text: The herbal preparation may interact with the antidepressant and increase the risk of serotonin toxicity or altered drug effectiveness
St John's wort always prevents antidepressant adverse effects
The herbal preparation has no pharmacological activity
The combination guarantees complete recovery from depression

questions.rationale: St John's wort has serotonergic activity and can interact with antidepressants, potentially causing serotonin toxicity; it also induces drug-metabolising enzymes that may reduce the effectiveness of other medicines. It should not be assumed to be harmless or universally beneficial.

questions.question_text: A client admitted with a psychotic disorder states that evil spirits are speaking to him and instructing him to harm his brother. What should the psychiatric nurse assess first?

choices.text: Whether the client has attended a religious service recently
The content of the voices, the client's intention to obey, access to weapons and immediate risk to others
Whether the client's relatives support traditional healing
The client's preferred type of religious music

questions.rationale: Command hallucinations involving harm to another person require immediate assessment of intent, capability, means and risk, followed by appropriate safety measures. Religious attendance, family preferences and music preferences may be explored later but do not establish the immediate level of danger.

questions.question_text: Which complementary intervention has evidence supporting its use as an adjunct to standard treatment for selected clients experiencing anxiety?

choices.text: Structured mindfulness-based relaxation exercises
Replacing prescribed medication with unregulated herbal mixtures
Prolonged social isolation
Sleep deprivation as a treatment for anxiety

questions.rationale: Structured mindfulness and relaxation interventions may reduce anxiety symptoms when used alongside appropriate clinical treatment. Unregulated medication substitution, isolation and sleep deprivation are not evidence-based anxiety treatments and may worsen mental health.

questions.question_text: A nurse receives a report that a prayer camp is withholding prescribed antipsychotic medication from residents and administering unidentified herbal mixtures. What is the most appropriate action?

choices.text: Ignore the report because the camp is privately managed
Arrange appropriate assessment of affected residents, investigate medication-related risks through authorised channels and facilitate safe psychiatric care
Encourage residents to consume larger quantities of the herbal preparations
Recommend that residents conceal their symptoms from healthcare workers

questions.rationale: Withholding prescribed medication and administering unidentified substances may result in relapse, toxicity and other serious complications, requiring clinical assessment and appropriate regulatory or safeguarding action. Private ownership does not remove responsibilities concerning patient safety and rights.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine and Psychotropic Drug Interactions
questions.question_text: A client taking clozapine begins using an unidentified herbal preparation and subsequently develops marked sedation, dizziness and confusion. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Reassure the client that herbal products cannot cause adverse reactions
Arrange urgent clinical assessment, review all substances taken and assess for clozapine toxicity
Recommend doubling the clozapine dose
Advise the client to stop attending psychiatric appointments

questions.rationale: New confusion and marked sedation in a client taking clozapine may indicate a serious adverse reaction or interaction and require urgent assessment. Unidentified herbal products can alter drug effects, making reassurance, dose escalation and discontinuation of follow-up unsafe.

questions.topic: Traditional Healing Practices and Mental Illness in Ghana
questions.question_text: A family takes a relative experiencing severe mania to a traditional healer before seeking hospital treatment. The client has not slept for four nights, is severely agitated and has become physically aggressive. What should the nurse recommend?

choices.text: Continue traditional treatment until the client becomes exhausted
Arrange urgent psychiatric assessment and emergency management because the presentation indicates severe mania with immediate safety concerns
Allow the client to remain unsupervised until the symptoms disappear
Discontinue all medical assessments because the family has selected traditional care

questions.rationale: Severe sleep deprivation, escalating agitation and physical aggression indicate a potentially dangerous manic episode requiring urgent psychiatric intervention and safety management. Delaying assessment or leaving the client unsupervised increases the risk of harm.

questions.topic: Patient Rights and Mental Health Legislation
questions.question_text: A person with a mental disorder is brought to a psychiatric facility after being physically restrained at a prayer camp. Which principle should guide the nurse's response under Ghana's mental health rights framework?

choices.text: The person's rights may be ignored because of the psychiatric diagnosis
The person retains dignity and legal rights and must receive care consistent with applicable safeguards and lawful procedures
Religious authorities automatically have unlimited authority over psychiatric treatment
Physical restraint should be used routinely whenever a client disagrees with treatment

questions.rationale: Act 846 provides a framework for protecting the dignity and rights of persons with mental disorders, including safeguards relating to treatment and care. Psychiatric diagnosis does not remove fundamental rights, and religious authority or disagreement with treatment does not justify unrestricted restraint.

questions.question_text: During an assessment, a client states that prayer provides emotional comfort while attending psychiatric treatment. What should the nurse's response be?

choices.text: Discourage prayer because it cannot contribute to emotional well-being
Respect the client's spiritual preference while ensuring that prayer complements rather than replaces necessary clinical treatment
Require the client to abandon all religious practices
Replace prescribed medication with religious activities

questions.rationale: Respecting a client's spiritual preferences supports holistic and culturally sensitive care when these practices do not compromise safety or evidence-based treatment. Rejecting religion or replacing necessary psychiatric interventions with prayer alone is inappropriate.

questions.topic: Herbal Medicine and Psychotropic Drug Interactions
questions.question_text: A client taking an antipsychotic reports using a traditional herbal mixture that causes additional drowsiness. Which pharmacological effect should the nurse consider?

choices.text: Possible additive central nervous system depressant effects
Guaranteed elimination of antipsychotic side effects
Complete prevention of drug absorption
Automatic development of antidepressant resistance

questions.rationale: Certain herbal substances may produce additive sedative effects when combined with antipsychotic medications, increasing the risk of excessive sedation and impaired functioning. The other options describe effects that cannot be assumed from the reported combination.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric nurse assesses four individuals attending a traditional healing centre. Which individual requires the most urgent intervention?

choices.text: A person with mild anxiety who reports feeling spiritually unsettled
A person with depression who requests information about counselling
A person with schizophrenia who is chained, severely dehydrated and intermittently unconscious
A person recovering from depression who wishes to attend religious services

questions.rationale: Chaining, severe dehydration and intermittent unconsciousness indicate immediate threats to life and require emergency medical stabilisation and safeguarding. The other individuals require appropriate mental health support but do not demonstrate the same immediate medical emergency.

questions.question_text: Which characteristic is a core diagnostic feature of autism spectrum disorder?

choices.text: Persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction, together with restricted or repetitive patterns of behaviour
Episodes of elevated mood occurring only during adolescence
Sudden loss of consciousness during stressful situations
Persistent hallucinations and persecutory delusions

questions.rationale: Autism spectrum disorder is characterised by persistent differences or deficits in social communication and interaction alongside restricted or repetitive behaviours, interests or activities. Mania, episodes of unconsciousness and psychotic symptoms are not defining diagnostic criteria for autism.

questions.question_text: A seven-year-old pupil in a Ghanaian primary school frequently leaves his seat, interrupts classmates, loses learning materials and struggles to complete classroom tasks. The behaviour has persisted for several months and occurs at home as well. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Autism spectrum disorder
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
Conduct disorder
Specific learning disorder

questions.rationale: Persistent inattention and hyperactive-impulsive behaviours occurring across multiple settings and impairing functioning suggest ADHD. Autism primarily involves social communication differences and restricted behaviours, while conduct disorder involves persistent violation of others' rights or social rules.

questions.question_text: Which approach is most appropriate when assessing the mental health of a six-year-old child?

choices.text: Interview the child without considering developmental level or family information
Use age-appropriate communication, observe behaviour and obtain relevant information from caregivers and other sources
Assume that all behavioural difficulties indicate a psychiatric disorder
Base the assessment exclusively on the child's academic performance

questions.rationale: Child psychiatric assessment requires developmentally appropriate communication, behavioural observation and information from caregivers and relevant settings. Ignoring developmental level, automatically diagnosing behavioural problems or relying solely on academic performance produces incomplete assessments.

questions.question_text: A child aged four years has significant limitations in intellectual functioning and difficulty acquiring age-appropriate adaptive skills such as communication, self-care and social participation. Which condition should be investigated?

choices.text: Intellectual disability
Specific phobia
Bipolar disorder
Obsessive-compulsive disorder

questions.rationale: Intellectual disability involves significant limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive behaviour with onset during the developmental period. Anxiety disorders, bipolar disorder and obsessive-compulsive disorder do not define this combination of developmental impairments.

questions.question_text: A child with autism becomes distressed whenever the classroom routine changes unexpectedly. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Introduce frequent unpredictable changes to increase tolerance
Use visual schedules, structured routines and advance preparation for transitions
Punish the child whenever distress occurs
Remove all communication aids from the classroom

questions.rationale: Predictable routines and visual supports can improve communication, reduce uncertainty and facilitate transitions for children with autism. Unpredictable changes, punishment and removing communication aids may increase distress and interfere with functioning.

questions.question_text: A ten-year-old child attending a paediatric clinic reports persistent sadness, social withdrawal and repeated statements that life is not worth living. What should the nurse prioritise?

choices.text: Assess suicide risk immediately using developmentally appropriate communication and establish safety
Advise the child to concentrate on schoolwork
Ignore the statements because children cannot experience suicidal thoughts
Arrange routine immunisation without further mental health assessment

questions.rationale: Children can experience suicidal thoughts, and statements indicating hopelessness require immediate developmentally appropriate risk assessment and safety planning. Dismissing the statements or concentrating on unrelated routine care may result in a preventable adverse outcome.

questions.question_text: Which intervention is commonly incorporated into the management of a school-aged child with ADHD?

choices.text: Structured behavioural interventions, consistent routines and appropriate educational support
Permanent exclusion from classroom activities
Deliberate sleep restriction
Punishment as the sole treatment approach

questions.rationale: ADHD management commonly includes behavioural interventions, parent training, educational accommodations and medication when clinically indicated. Exclusion, sleep restriction and punishment alone do not address the neurodevelopmental condition and may worsen functioning.

questions.question_text: A nurse assesses an adolescent who reports hearing voices commenting on his activities. What is the most important additional assessment?

choices.text: The adolescent's favourite recreational activity
The voices' content, frequency, associated distress, command features and risk of self-harm or harm to others
The adolescent's preferred school subject
The number of friends the adolescent has without further exploration

questions.rationale: Auditory hallucinations require detailed assessment of their characteristics and potential safety implications, particularly command content and associated intentions. Recreational preferences and school interests may contribute to the psychosocial history but do not establish the immediate clinical risk.

questions.question_text: A child with intellectual disability experiences a seizure lasting six minutes in a paediatric ward. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Protect the child from injury, maintain airway positioning, time the seizure and activate emergency management
Force an object into the child's mouth
Restrain all four limbs firmly
Offer oral medication while the child is convulsing

questions.rationale: A prolonged seizure requires immediate seizure first aid, airway protection and emergency management according to protocol. Placing objects in the mouth, forceful restraint and administering oral medication during convulsions can cause serious injury or aspiration.

questions.question_text: Which finding would most strongly support a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder rather than ADHD alone?

choices.text: Persistent deficits in reciprocal social communication accompanied by restricted and repetitive behaviours
Occasional difficulty completing homework
Increased physical activity during outdoor play
Difficulty sitting still during a single classroom lesson

questions.rationale: Persistent social communication difficulties combined with restricted or repetitive behaviours are central features of autism spectrum disorder. Inattention, excessive activity and isolated classroom difficulties are not sufficient to distinguish autism from ADHD or other developmental concerns.

questions.question_text: A fifteen-year-old adolescent presents with persistent low mood, loss of interest, poor concentration, feelings of worthlessness and declining school performance for six weeks. Which condition is most likely?

choices.text: Major depressive disorder
Autism spectrum disorder
Specific phobia
Acute delirium

questions.rationale: Persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, worthlessness, impaired concentration and functional decline over several weeks suggest a depressive episode requiring comprehensive assessment. Autism, specific phobia and delirium have different defining clinical features and do not adequately explain the complete presentation.

questions.question_text: A nurse observes bruises on a child admitted with anxiety and behavioural difficulties. During a private interview, the child discloses repeated physical abuse by a caregiver. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Confront the caregiver aggressively before assessing the child
Ensure the child's immediate safety, document findings objectively and activate appropriate child protection procedures
Tell the child to resolve the conflict independently
Ignore the disclosure because the caregiver is the legal guardian

questions.rationale: Suspected child abuse requires immediate safeguarding, objective documentation, appropriate reporting and referral in accordance with child protection procedures. Aggressive confrontation, placing responsibility on the child or ignoring the disclosure may expose the child to further harm.

questions.question_text: A twelve-year-old child develops sudden confusion, fluctuating attention and visual hallucinations after several days of high fever. Which condition should the nurse suspect?

choices.text: Delirium associated with an acute medical condition
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
Autism spectrum disorder
Specific learning disorder

questions.rationale: Acute confusion, fluctuating attention and hallucinations following fever suggest delirium secondary to an underlying medical condition. ADHD, autism and specific learning disorder are not characterised by an acute fluctuating disturbance of consciousness and attention.

questions.question_text: An adolescent with major depression tells the nurse that he has swallowed several tablets with the intention of dying. He is becoming drowsy. What is the immediate nursing priority?

choices.text: Conduct a detailed family assessment before providing care
Initiate emergency overdose management, assess airway, breathing and circulation, and arrange urgent medical intervention
Begin group counselling immediately
Allow the adolescent to sleep without observation

questions.rationale: An intentional overdose with increasing drowsiness represents a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate medical stabilisation and overdose management. Psychosocial assessment and counselling are necessary after the adolescent's physical condition has been stabilised.

questions.question_text: A child taking prescribed methylphenidate for ADHD develops reduced appetite, difficulty sleeping and weight loss. What should the nurse recommend?

choices.text: Increase the medication dose without medical review
Arrange clinical review to assess adverse effects, growth and the medication regimen
Discontinue all follow-up appointments
Assure the parents that weight loss requires no monitoring

questions.rationale: Methylphenidate can cause appetite suppression, insomnia and reduced weight gain, making monitoring of growth and clinical review essential. Unauthorised dose escalation, abandonment of follow-up and failure to monitor growth are inappropriate.

questions.question_text: A community nurse identifies a three-year-old child who has not developed expected language skills and has limited social interaction. What is the most appropriate next step?

choices.text: Wait until the child starts primary school before investigating
Arrange comprehensive developmental assessment and early intervention referral
Assume the child has a psychiatric disorder without assessment
Advise the parents to stop communicating with the child until speech develops

questions.rationale: Developmental delays require early identification, comprehensive assessment and timely intervention to improve communication and functional outcomes. Delaying assessment, making unsupported diagnoses and restricting communication may worsen developmental difficulties.

questions.question_text: A paediatric nurse assesses four children. Which child requires the most immediate intervention?

choices.text: A child with autism who becomes distressed by loud classroom noise
A child with ADHD who frequently interrupts classroom activities
An adolescent with depression who has a specific suicide plan and access to the intended means
A child with developmental delay who requires assistance with dressing

questions.rationale: An adolescent with a specific suicide plan and access to the intended means presents an immediate threat to life and requires emergency risk management. Sensory distress, ADHD-related behavioural difficulties and adaptive functioning limitations require care but are not equivalent immediate threats.

questions.question_text: What is the main objective of integrating mental health services into primary healthcare in Ghana?

choices.text: To restrict psychiatric services to specialised hospitals
To improve accessible, early and continuous mental healthcare within community-based health services
To eliminate the need for psychiatric specialists
To transfer all psychiatric responsibilities to traditional healers

questions.rationale: Integration of mental health into primary healthcare improves accessibility, early identification, treatment continuity and community participation. It does not eliminate specialist services or transfer clinical responsibilities to unregulated providers.

questions.question_text: A community health nurse at a CHPS compound identifies an adult who reports persistent sadness, loss of interest and poor sleep. Which screening approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use an appropriate validated depression screening instrument and arrange clinical assessment when indicated
Diagnose schizophrenia based exclusively on the reported sadness
Prescribe antidepressants without further assessment
Ignore the symptoms unless the individual develops hallucinations

questions.rationale: Validated screening tools can identify individuals who may have depression and require further clinical assessment. Screening does not independently establish a diagnosis or authorise treatment, and hallucinations are not a prerequisite for depression assessment.

questions.question_text: Which activity represents primary prevention in community mental healthcare?

choices.text: Providing mental health education and resilience-building programmes before psychiatric disorders develop
Rehabilitating clients after prolonged psychiatric hospitalisation
Providing treatment to individuals experiencing an acute psychotic episode
Managing established complications of chronic schizophrenia

questions.rationale: Primary prevention aims to reduce the incidence of mental disorders by addressing risk factors and strengthening protective factors before illness develops. Acute treatment is an intervention for established illness, while rehabilitation and management of complications are secondary or tertiary interventions.

questions.question_text: During a home visit, a community nurse discovers that a client with depression has written a suicide note and purchased a pesticide. What should the nurse do first?

choices.text: Arrange a routine appointment for the following month
Conduct an immediate suicide risk assessment, ensure safety and arrange emergency mental health intervention
Advise the client to remain alone until the feelings disappear
Recommend exercise as the only intervention

questions.rationale: A suicide note and acquisition of a potentially lethal substance indicate an acute and serious suicide risk requiring immediate safety measures and emergency assessment. Routine follow-up, isolation and exercise alone are inadequate responses to imminent suicide risk.

questions.question_text: Which institution is responsible for overseeing the implementation and coordination of mental health services under Ghana's Mental Health Act, 2012 (Act 846)?

choices.text: Mental Health Authority
Ghana Immigration Service
National Commission for Civic Education
Ghana Revenue Authority

questions.rationale: The Mental Health Authority provides leadership and oversight for mental health service delivery under Act 846. The other institutions perform functions related to immigration, civic education and revenue administration.

questions.question_text: A nurse working at a rural CHPS compound identifies a person with suspected psychosis. The nearest psychiatric specialist is located several kilometres away. What is the most appropriate approach?

choices.text: Provide an initial assessment, address immediate safety concerns and coordinate referral to an appropriate mental health service
Keep the person at home without clinical follow-up
Attempt to manage severe psychosis independently without appropriate support
Refer the person exclusively to an informal religious institution

questions.rationale: Primary healthcare integration involves early identification, appropriate initial management, safety assessment and coordinated referral within the mental health system. Abandoning care, practising beyond competence or relying exclusively on informal services may delay necessary specialist intervention.

questions.question_text: Which activity best demonstrates secondary prevention in community mental healthcare?

choices.text: Early screening and identification of depressive symptoms among community members
Long-term vocational rehabilitation following psychiatric illness
Public education before any mental health symptoms develop
Long-term residential support for individuals with chronic psychiatric disabilities

questions.rationale: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt intervention to reduce disease progression and complications. Public education before illness develops represents primary prevention, while vocational rehabilitation and long-term disability support are tertiary prevention activities.

questions.question_text: A community nurse receives a report that an adolescent has posted a message indicating an intention to die that night. What is the most appropriate initial response?

choices.text: Assume the message is intended to attract attention
Establish immediate contact, assess suicide risk, determine the adolescent's location and arrange urgent safety intervention
Wait until the adolescent attends the next scheduled clinic appointment
Share the message publicly to discourage similar behaviour

questions.rationale: An expressed intention to die at a specific time must be treated as a potential emergency requiring immediate contact, risk assessment and safety intervention. Dismissal, delayed review and public disclosure may increase the danger and violate confidentiality.

questions.question_text: A district public health team plans a programme to reduce stigma towards people with mental disorders. Which intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Promoting community education, contact with people with lived experience and accurate information about mental illness
Discouraging people with psychiatric histories from participating in community activities
Presenting mental illness exclusively as a permanent condition of dangerousness
Preventing discharged clients from returning to employment

questions.rationale: Community education combined with meaningful contact can challenge stereotypes and improve acceptance of people with mental disorders. Exclusion, fear-based messaging and employment discrimination reinforce stigma and undermine social inclusion.

questions.question_text: A client with schizophrenia repeatedly misses follow-up appointments because transport costs are high. Which public health nursing intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Discharge the client for failure to attend appointments
Coordinate accessible community follow-up, assess available NHIS benefits and link the client with appropriate support services
Require the client to attend only Accra Psychiatric Hospital
Advise the client to discontinue psychiatric treatment

questions.rationale: Community-based follow-up and assessment of available financial and transport support can reduce barriers to continuity of care. Discharge, unnecessary distant referrals and treatment discontinuation increase the likelihood of relapse and poor outcomes.

questions.question_text: A community nurse screens four individuals during a health outreach programme. Which individual requires the most urgent intervention?

choices.text: An adult who reports occasional worry about employment
An adult who reports difficulty sleeping during examination periods
An individual with depression who reports a specific suicide plan and immediate access to the intended means
An adult who requests information about stress management

questions.rationale: A specific suicide plan and immediate access to the intended means indicate a potentially imminent threat to life and require emergency intervention. General worry, situational sleep difficulties and requests for health education require assessment but do not represent the same immediate danger.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the purpose of community mental health services?

choices.text: To provide accessible mental health promotion, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and follow-up within communities
To eliminate all psychiatric hospitals and specialist services
To restrict psychiatric care to individuals with severe psychotic disorders
To transfer mental healthcare responsibilities exclusively to families

questions.rationale: Community mental health services provide a continuum of care, including prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and continuity of support close to where people live. They complement specialist services rather than eliminate them or transfer clinical responsibilities to families.

questions.question_text: A community nurse discovers that a client with schizophrenia has developed severe rigidity, fever and altered consciousness after starting an antipsychotic medication. What is the priority action?

choices.text: Arrange urgent medical assessment for suspected neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Recommend additional exercise to reduce rigidity
Wait for the next routine home visit
Encourage the client to take additional antipsychotic medication

questions.rationale: Fever, severe rigidity and altered consciousness in a person taking antipsychotic medication suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a life-threatening medical emergency. Delayed assessment, exercise and additional antipsychotic medication may worsen the condition.

questions.question_text: A public health nurse identifies increasing suicide attempts among adolescents in a district. Which intervention best represents a comprehensive community-level prevention strategy?

choices.text: Combining mental health education, early identification, accessible referral pathways, crisis response and responsible media engagement
Restricting all mental health information from schools
Relying exclusively on hospital admission after suicide attempts
Publicly identifying adolescents who have previously attempted suicide

questions.rationale: Comprehensive suicide prevention combines population-level promotion, early detection, accessible services, crisis intervention and responsible communication. Restricting education, relying only on post-attempt hospital care and publicly identifying individuals increase missed prevention opportunities and stigma.

questions.question_text: A district health director is planning mental health promotion activities for secondary schools. Which intervention is most appropriate?

choices.text: Providing age-appropriate mental health literacy, emotional regulation skills and pathways for confidential help-seeking
Punishing students who disclose emotional difficulties
Discouraging teachers from referring students with behavioural changes
Discussing individual students' psychiatric histories during public assemblies

questions.rationale: School-based mental health promotion improves knowledge, coping skills, early identification and access to support while respecting confidentiality. Punishment, discouraging referrals and public disclosure may increase stigma and prevent students from seeking care.

questions.question_text: A nurse screens a pregnant woman at a community antenatal outreach programme and identifies persistent low mood, anhedonia and hopelessness. The woman also reports thoughts of self-harm. What should the nurse do?

choices.text: Treat the findings as normal pregnancy-related emotional changes
Conduct an immediate safety assessment and arrange urgent maternal mental health evaluation
Advise the woman to stop attending antenatal services
Recommend herbal preparations without assessing the woman's condition

questions.rationale: Depressive symptoms accompanied by self-harm thoughts during pregnancy require immediate risk assessment and appropriate maternal mental health intervention. Normalising the symptoms, discontinuing antenatal care and recommending unassessed herbal preparations may delay essential treatment.

questions.question_text: A district mental health coordinator reviews four community cases. Which case should be escalated immediately to emergency services?

choices.text: A client with stable schizophrenia requesting vocational rehabilitation
A client with mild anxiety requesting counselling
A client with acute confusion, high fever and severe dehydration
A client with depression who wishes to join a support group

questions.rationale: Acute confusion, fever and severe dehydration may indicate delirium associated with a serious medical condition and require emergency medical assessment. Stable rehabilitation needs, mild anxiety and support-group requests can be managed through appropriate routine community services.

questions.question_text: A private mental health clinic in Accra wants to attract individuals experiencing depression and anxiety. Which marketing strategy is most appropriate?

choices.text: Advertising guaranteed cures for every psychiatric condition
Providing accurate information about available services, qualified professionals, referral pathways and treatment approaches
Using frightening images of people experiencing psychosis to attract attention
Promising that clients will recover within three days

questions.rationale: Ethical mental health marketing communicates accurate service information and realistic expectations while supporting informed decision-making. Guaranteed cures, fear-based images and unrealistic recovery promises are misleading and may reinforce stigma.

questions.question_text: Which principle should guide the marketing of psychiatric services?

choices.text: Truthfulness and transparency in communicating service benefits and limitations
Exaggerating treatment outcomes to increase client numbers
Concealing service costs until treatment has started
Using client information without permission to attract customers

questions.rationale: Ethical marketing requires truthful information, transparency and respect for patient autonomy. Exaggerated claims, concealed costs and unauthorised disclosure violate professional and ethical responsibilities.

questions.question_text: A mental health entrepreneur plans a social media campaign to encourage young Ghanaians to seek help for depression. Which message is most appropriate?

choices.text: Depression is a sign of weakness that should be hidden from society.
Depression is a treatable mental health condition, and seeking professional support is an important step towards recovery.
People with depression should avoid professional healthcare.
Only individuals with severe psychosis require mental health services.

questions.rationale: Accurate, recovery-oriented communication normalises help-seeking and challenges misconceptions about depression. The other messages promote stigma, discourage treatment and incorrectly restrict mental healthcare to psychotic disorders.

questions.question_text: An entrepreneur intends to establish a mental health support centre in a rural Ghanaian district. Which consideration should receive priority during business planning?

choices.text: Assessing community needs, service gaps, regulatory requirements, qualified staffing and financial sustainability
Selecting a location based exclusively on the availability of entertainment facilities
Employing untrained individuals to provide psychiatric diagnoses
Advertising services before establishing appropriate clinical governance

questions.rationale: Sustainable mental healthcare entrepreneurship requires needs assessment, regulatory compliance, competent personnel, appropriate governance and financial planning. Entertainment facilities, unqualified clinical practice and premature advertising do not establish a safe or viable service.

questions.question_text: A mental health clinic wants to publish a testimonial from a former client who received treatment for schizophrenia. What should management do before publication?

choices.text: Publish the testimonial immediately because the client's treatment has ended
Obtain informed, voluntary and appropriately documented consent and protect the client's privacy and dignity
Include the client's full medical records to increase credibility
Ask another client to provide consent on the individual's behalf without legal authority

questions.rationale: Patient testimonials require informed and voluntary consent, appropriate privacy safeguards and protection against exploitation or coercion. Ending treatment does not remove confidentiality obligations, and disclosure of medical records or unauthorised third-party consent is inappropriate.

questions.question_text: A mental health clinic receives repeated complaints about long waiting times and poor communication. Which management response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Ignore complaints because psychiatric clients are unlikely to change providers
Analyse feedback, identify service deficiencies and implement measurable quality improvement measures
Remove all complaint channels from the clinic
Blame clients for failing to understand the service system

questions.rationale: Service quality improvement uses client feedback to identify operational problems and strengthen patient experience and continuity of care. Ignoring complaints, removing feedback channels and blaming clients undermine trust and relationship management.

questions.question_text: Which marketing concept focuses on developing long-term, mutually beneficial relationships between a healthcare organisation and its clients?

choices.text: Relationship marketing
Product elimination
Price discrimination
Market withdrawal

questions.rationale: Relationship marketing focuses on maintaining long-term client relationships through trust, satisfaction, communication and service quality. Product elimination, price discrimination and market withdrawal do not describe the development of sustainable client relationships.

questions.question_text: A private psychiatric clinic advertises that its treatment guarantees permanent recovery from schizophrenia. What is the most appropriate professional response?

choices.text: Support the advertisement because it attracts more clients
Withdraw or correct the misleading claim and replace it with accurate, evidence-based information
Increase the advertisement's visibility through paid promotions
Encourage clients to discontinue prescribed treatment after one visit

questions.rationale: Psychiatric treatment outcomes vary, and a guarantee of permanent recovery is scientifically misleading and ethically unacceptable. Correcting the claim protects the public from misinformation, whereas increasing its reach or encouraging treatment discontinuation creates additional risks.

questions.question_text: A marketing team is designing a poster for a community mental health programme. Which image and message combination is most appropriate?

choices.text: An image portraying psychiatric clients as violent, accompanied by a warning to avoid them
An image of people participating in ordinary community activities, accompanied by a message encouraging early mental health support
An image showing psychiatric treatment as punishment
An image suggesting that mental illness results exclusively from spiritual weakness

questions.rationale: Inclusive imagery and accurate help-seeking messages challenge stereotypes and promote social acceptance. Fear-based, punitive and spiritually discriminatory representations reinforce stigma and discourage access to evidence-based services.

questions.question_text: An entrepreneur plans to introduce a digital platform that connects people experiencing psychological distress with qualified mental health professionals in Ghana. Which feature is most important?

choices.text: Secure communication, confidentiality safeguards, appropriate professional verification and emergency referral pathways
Public display of every user's psychiatric diagnosis
Unrestricted access to clinical records by advertisers
Automatic psychiatric diagnosis without clinical oversight

questions.rationale: A digital mental health platform must protect sensitive information, verify professional qualifications and provide safe pathways for emergencies. Public disclosure, advertising access to clinical records and unsupported automated diagnosis compromise confidentiality and patient safety.

questions.question_text: A clinic receptionist receives a telephone call from a journalist requesting the name of a prominent individual receiving psychiatric treatment. What should the receptionist do?

choices.text: Disclose the information because the caller works for the media
Refuse unauthorised disclosure and direct the request through the clinic's authorised confidentiality procedures
Confirm the diagnosis but withhold the treatment details
Send the client's prescription through social media

questions.rationale: A person's attendance at a psychiatric clinic and associated health information are confidential and cannot be disclosed without appropriate legal authority or valid consent. Media employment does not create permission to access patient information, and partial disclosure remains a confidentiality breach.

questions.question_text: A mental health entrepreneur discovers that residents of a rural community avoid psychiatric services because they fear being labelled as mentally ill. Which marketing strategy is most appropriate?

choices.text: Organise confidential community education, engage trusted stakeholders and communicate the availability of accessible mental health services
Publicly identify individuals who have attended psychiatric clinics
Use threatening advertisements about untreated mental illness
Restrict information about services to urban communities

questions.rationale: Confidential education and engagement with trusted community stakeholders can reduce stigma and improve awareness of accessible care. Public identification, threatening messages and geographical exclusion reinforce discrimination and reduce service uptake.

questions.question_text: A private mental health facility wants to measure whether its marketing campaign has improved access to psychiatric services. Which indicator is most appropriate?

choices.text: The number of relevant enquiries, completed referrals and clients accessing appropriate services
The number of advertisements printed without considering audience response
The number of staff members who view the campaign internally
The number of unrelated social media comments received

questions.rationale: Relevant enquiries, completed referrals and service utilisation provide measurable indicators of whether marketing improves access to mental healthcare. Advertising volume, internal staff views and unrelated comments do not independently demonstrate improved service uptake.

questions.question_text: A mental health entrepreneur plans to use a former client's photograph and psychiatric diagnosis in an online advertisement. The client previously agreed verbally during a treatment session but has not signed a marketing consent document. What should the entrepreneur do?

choices.text: Publish the advertisement because verbal agreement during treatment is always sufficient
Obtain separate, informed and voluntary marketing consent, ensure privacy safeguards and comply with applicable professional and data protection requirements
Publish the photograph but remove the client's name
Ask clinic employees to decide whether the client should be identified

questions.rationale: Using identifiable health information for marketing requires appropriate consent and safeguards separate from routine clinical care, particularly because of the sensitivity of psychiatric information. Removing a name may not prevent identification, and employees cannot replace the client's consent.

questions.question_text: A mental health startup has limited financial resources but wants to expand access to counselling in underserved Ghanaian communities. Which business model is most appropriate?

choices.text: Developing partnerships with existing health facilities, qualified professionals and community organisations while using sustainable service financing
Offering psychiatric diagnosis through untrained sales representatives
Charging clients for services that the organisation cannot provide
Avoiding partnerships to prevent professional accountability

questions.rationale: Strategic partnerships can extend service reach, improve access to qualified personnel and support financial sustainability. Untrained diagnosis, misleading charges and avoidance of accountability undermine safe and viable mental health entrepreneurship.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric clinic discovers that an employee has shared a client's depression diagnosis in a public WhatsApp group. What should management do first?

choices.text: Ignore the incident because the information has already been shared
Contain the disclosure, assess its impact, protect the affected client and initiate appropriate incident reporting and investigation procedures
Share additional clinical details to explain the diagnosis
Publish the employee's personal information to punish the individual

questions.rationale: A confidentiality breach requires immediate containment, assessment of potential harm, protection of the affected client and appropriate investigation and reporting under applicable policies and law. Ignoring the breach, expanding disclosure or retaliatory publication creates further ethical and privacy violations.

questions.question_text: A mental health clinic receives a complaint from a client who believes that staff members treated him disrespectfully because of his history of schizophrenia. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Dismiss the complaint because psychiatric clients may misinterpret staff behaviour
Listen respectfully, investigate the complaint fairly, address any discriminatory conduct and communicate the outcome through appropriate channels
Remove the client from the clinic's service register
Publicly discuss the client's complaint to discourage future complaints

questions.rationale: Respectful complaint management supports accountability, patient dignity, trust and continuous service improvement. Dismissing complaints based on diagnosis, excluding the client or disclosing the complaint publicly constitutes inappropriate and potentially discriminatory practice.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric facility advertises a new service claiming that clients can obtain immediate treatment without assessment, even when experiencing severe suicidal thoughts or acute psychosis. What is the most appropriate corrective action?

choices.text: Maintain the advertisement because rapid access increases customer satisfaction
Correct the advertisement to explain appropriate service eligibility, clinical assessment requirements and emergency referral arrangements
Promise that every client will receive identical treatment regardless of clinical condition
Remove all information about emergency psychiatric services

questions.rationale: Mental health marketing must communicate accurate service capabilities and appropriate pathways for urgent psychiatric emergencies. Promising treatment without assessment or identical interventions for all clients creates unsafe expectations, while concealing emergency information may delay lifesaving care.
